interpretation.state_model: bounded pure-state statevector; at most 4 qubits
interpretation.numeric_semantics: complex amplitudes represented as pairs of Python Fraction values; irrational and trigonometric coefficients and post-measurement normalization are deterministically rationalized by the implementation, so arithmetic is exact only within that encoded rational approximation model
interpretation.parameter_grammar: restricted numeric/pi literals implemented by qasm_matrix._parse_angle; U requires exactly three comma-separated supported angles; executable source statements are semicolon-terminated and unitary wires use indexed q[i] references
interpretation.global_phase_policy: not_applicable_to_instrument_semantics; unitary gate actions retain represented complex phase within the declared rational approximation model
interpretation.measurement: c[i] = measure q[j]; computational-basis projective measurement with explicit collapse; the destination must be a declared in-range indexed bit; nondeterministic outcomes fail closed
interpretation.classical_state: explicit indexed measurement-bit names populated before use
interpretation.feedforward: if (<measured-bit> == 1) <supported terminated gate>; indexed bits such as c[1] are supported; predicates must reference declared measured bits; no else or loops
interpretation.branch_completeness: single deterministic execution only; nondeterministic branch enumeration is outside this profile

parser_or_interpreter.trust_role: externally_trusted bounded operational interpreter; not kernel-checked

notes: Executable bounded operational profile for deterministic-branch dynamic fragments. Source syntax requires a leading OPENQASM 3.0; header, terminated recognized statements, exactly one vector qubit register named q, indexed q[i] wire references, and explicitly declared bounds-checked bit registers. Unitariy gate actions are delegated to the canonical LSB v2 gate semantics, including correct CZ/CP behavior with spectator qubits. It is not full OpenQASM dynamic-circuit semantics, density-operator/channel semantics, hardware semantics, or an arbitrary-input teleportation proof. Only syntactically recognized include "..."; lines are skipped, and they are not semantically imported.
